issues.legal_issue: A single lease of accommodation for both residential and non-residential purposes does not prevent eviction when the landlord establishes the applicable bona fide need for each part.
material_facts: The tenant occupied a building under an integral lease for both residential use and operation of a cloth business.
The landlord sought the ground floor to operate a chemist shop and the first floor for residence.
The final court of fact found both requirements bona fide, and that finding was not challenged in the High Court or in the appeal to the Supreme Court.
The tenant appealed against the eviction decree.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed and the eviction order was upheld because the residential and non-residential parts each constituted accommodation and the landlord had established the corresponding bona fide requirements.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, accommodation includes a building or part of a building, whether residential or non-residential. Sections 12(1)(e) and 12(1)(f) permit eviction respectively for a bona fide residential requirement and a bona fide requirement to continue or start a business, subject to the statutory conditions concerning other reasonably suitable accommodation. An integral lease may have dual purposes without being impermissibly split: eviction may be ordered for the relevant residential and non-residential parts when the respective grounds are established. S. Sanyal v. Gian Chand, [1968] 1 S.C.R. 536, was distinguished because the case involved no splitting of the contract.

predicates.appeal_against_eviction_decree: The tenant brought an appeal challenging an eviction decree.
predicates.integral_lease_has_residential_and_busin: The tenant occupied the accommodation under one integral lease for both residential use and a business purpose.
predicates.landlord_bona_fide_needs_both_parts: The landlord established a bona fide need to use the residential part as a residence and the non-residential part for a business.
predicates.factual_finding_of_bona_fide_need_is_unc: The finding that the landlord had the asserted bona fide needs was not challenged in the subsequent appeals.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an eviction decree concerning an integral dual-purpose lease, and the landlord's bona fide need for both parts is established by an unchallenged finding, the eviction order is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant may be given time to relocate before an eviction order is executed when the circumstances make immediate relocation difficult.
material_facts: The tenant had operated a thriving cloth business with established goodwill for nearly thirty years.
The Court noted the scarcity of accommodation and the difficulty of finding suitable alternative premises.
The Court dismissed the tenant's appeal but postponed execution of the eviction order to allow time to secure alternative accommodation.
issues.conclusion: The Court deferred execution of the eviction order to give the tenant time to find suitable alternative accommodation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised equitable discretion in light of the tenant's established business and the stated scarcity of accommodation, while leaving the eviction order in force.

predicates.appeal_against_eviction_decree_is_dismis: The tenant's appeal against the eviction decree is dismissed.

predicates.suitable_alternative_accommodation_is_di: Suitable alternative accommodation is difficult to obtain because accommodation is scarce.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal is dismissed but the tenant has a longstanding thriving business and suitable alternative accommodation is difficult to find, execution is deferred to allow relocation.
